scope: main.py, split_lab_test.py, split_patient_info.py, split_dignosis.py, split_visit_record.py and utils.py
finding: The scripts read a table named final_preprocessed_data.csv, partition fields, replace identifiers and translate labels. They contain no hospital eligibility query and no numerical laboratory-standardization implementation.
implication: These files document downstream preparation only.

scope: 939 columns; source retained within the institution
finding: Four diagnosis-text sources are present: 门（急）诊诊断, 出院主要诊断名称1, 病理诊断, 上次诊断. No explicit complication-screen field, eligibility flag, original unit or reference-interval metadata are present.
implication: The upstream inclusion query and original physical-scale units cannot be recovered from this header.
source: Institutional extract; aggregate layout reported in outputs/quality_control_report.json

finding: The release retains the supplied patient cohort and copies each retained laboratory cell unchanged. Of 908 candidate laboratory columns, 137 wholly empty columns are omitted and 771 are retained.
implication: The source-extract-to-release operation is verified for every retained variable. This is separate from the original hospital conversion.

material: Clinical eligibility definition supplied by the data providers
scope: Adults aged at least 18 years and eight cardiovascular comorbidity categories
finding: At least one of coronary heart disease, hypertension, heart failure, arrhythmia, valvular heart disease, cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease or vascular disease is required. Other diseases are allowed. Heart failure qualifies independently of cardiomyopathy.
implication: Clinical OR criteria, ICD-10 use and Chinese synonyms are confirmed by SCH through the authors on 11 November 2026. The executable query and exact code-level implementation are not retained in the extract.
source: Author-relayed SCH confirmation on 11 November 2026; outputs/eligibility_rule_dictionary.csv

finding: 305 fields contain negative values; 466 contain values outside [0,1]. No field simultaneously has mean zero and population standard deviation one within 0.000001 on the released observations.
implication: Observed distributions do not identify a unique original transformation, including transformations fitted to another population. No conversion parameters are disclosed.

finding: 359982 records (99.92%) agreed within 1 g/L under the validation model, with median absolute difference 0.092 g/L. This supports the inference that negative hemoglobin scores likely indicate measurements below a reference lower limit.
implication: Aggregate evidence supports a hemoglobin-specific interpretation; it does not verify the original implementation for all laboratory variables.
source: outputs/hemoglobin_interpretation_summary.json; confidential parameters supplied separately to the editor

finding: Reference-interval linear models have internal-consistency support for 27 well-observed fields and consistency for two sparse variants; 269 released fields are constant. Ten blood-count and protein relationships were assessed in held-out patients.
implication: Field-level model evidence is reported without asserting independent source-implementation verification. Detailed mappings are confidential.
